program_dates: Master's programmes starting September 2027 (13 or 25 months of living allowance, by programme length)

Not older than 35 on 1 September 2027
GPA of 7.5 out of 10 or higher, 'equivalent to a minimum of 75% out of 100% or 3 out of 4'
Never participated in a degree-seeking higher education programme in the Netherlands

Transcript showing GPA of 7.5 or higher, with an explanation of the grading system
One reference letter dated no earlier than February 2026, with the referee's work email and phone

Log in with the UM student account and submit the scholarship form by 1 February 2027 (one submission only)

Flights are not covered; accommodation is paid from the stipend
No Master of Public Policy or logistics MSc among participating programmes; business options include MSc International Business, Financial Economics and Learning and Development in Organisations

Degree from a highly ranked European university

title: Gates Cambridge Scholarship (2027-28 entry)
organization: Gates Cambridge Trust, University of Cambridge
overview: Full-cost scholarships for outstanding applicants from outside the UK to pursue a PhD, MLitt or one-year postgraduate course (such as an MPhil) at the University of Cambridge.

program_dates: Fellowship year April 2027 to March 2028; Opening Assembly May 2027 via Zoom; Closing Assembly June 2028 (in person only if funding is secured)
deadline_text: November 11, 2026: Application deadline (applications and all accompanying materials must be submitted by 22:00 Coordinated Universal Time). Application opened October 1, 2026.
funding_details: 'We do not offer funding for projects.'

The Fellowship page says they aim to give Fellows an in-person experience and 'cover all costs for attending the Assembly such as visa fees, travel, and lodging', but the 2027 Opening Assembly is on Zoom and the 2028 in-person Assembly depends on funding
eligibility: 20 to 36 years old as of 1 April 2027
Fluency in written and spoken English
Current engagement with, or well-articulated plans for, a social change project
In-depth knowledge of the community, preferably at least one year of experience (the FAQ says at least six months)
About 12 hours per month
'Applicants can be enrolled in undergraduate or graduate studies, or not at all'
nationality_requirements: No nationality restriction: 'changemakers from around the world'
experience_requirement: At least six months of experience with the community served

Apply on apply.dalailamafellows.com by 11 November 2026, 22:00 UTC
eligibility_reason: Age, English and the absence of any degree requirement are met. Eligibility hinges on having, or credibly planning, a community social-change project with at least six months of community experience, which the profile does not record.
potential_issues: Not a travel opportunity in 2027: the Opening Assembly is on Zoom
The old domain dalailamafellows.org redirects to an unrelated site; use dalailamafellows.com only
relevance_reason: Free and open without degree conditions, but it rewards an existing community project and brings no money or travel in the first year.
action: Apply before 11 November 2026 only if you lead, or have a concrete plan for, a community project you have worked with for at least six months. Attend an information session first.
notes: Previously on the research watchlist: the programme's current host is dalailamafellows.com (contact address at virginia.edu).

organization: Dalai Lama Fellows (hosted with the University of Virginia)
overview: A one-year, largely virtual fellowship for 15-20 changemakers aged 20-36 who lead or plan a social change project in their community, with training in ethical and compassionate leadership.
